display.title: What Is a Mitzvah? The Lesson of Chanukah
display.summary_short: A mitzvah is a commandment from Hashem, our Commander-in-Chief. Uncle Yossi explains why that is exactly what Chanukah is about.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Chanukah show of 5742, answering a listener's letter. Uncle Yossi explains that the word mitzvah means a commandment, and the Commander is Hashem. Mitzvos are lovely to do, but we do them because Hashem commanded us. That is the heart of Chanukah: the Greeks did not mind Jews doing "good deeds", but would not let them be called commandments from G-d. Matisyahu, Yochanan, Yehudah HaMaccabi and others united the Jewish people to fight back, knowing that the Jewish nation depends on learning the Torah as G-d's Torah. A handful of outnumbered Jews won with trust in Hashem. Each night, as we light the menorah, we also light a spark in our soul that gives us strength all year to fight the yetzer hara, learn more Torah and do more mitzvos.
display.lesson: We do mitzvos because Hashem commanded them, and each Chanukah light gives us strength against the yetzer hara.
